rule: EXACT description of the implementation. Every 64-hex value (matched case-insensitively) in a file whose extension is .json (matched case-insensitively) is checked. For a value under key K the target is selected in this order: (1) NAME-AFFINE - if K ends with one of _sha256/_sha1/_sha/_hash/_digest, the target is the first present non-empty string among {stem}_ref, {stem}_path, {stem}_file, {stem}_artifact, {stem}_artifact_ref, {stem}_locator, {stem}, where stem is K without that suffix; when any is present the authoritative list in (2) is NOT consulted; (2) otherwise the first present non-empty string among the authoritative keys: path, file, target, artifact, artifact_ref, path_or_external_exact_ref, ref, historical_contract_ref, historical_compiled_prompt_ref, historical_calibration_artifact, proof_artifact, contract_path, rank1_authority_path, current_rank1_authority_path, plus K itself when K looks path-like (contains a slash, ends .json, or matches <hex>:<path>). The FIRST selected target that RESOLVES is authoritative: it must equal the value, and later targets are not examined. A selected target that does NOT resolve raises an error only if it is a relative path or a git reference AND no other selected target resolved. An absolute target whose basename is not uniquely in-tree is accepted when the value matches an in-tree or allowlisted blob. If no target resolved, the value must match the sha256 of some in-tree file or be in the external/historical allowlist. Failures inside a superseded/ scope are collected in superseded_scope_stale_references rather than raised.
known_limitations: path-like strings that are not SELECTED targets are not examined: repo slugs such as 'shw097-team/SWOF', a descriptive 'locator' like 'branch X @ <sha>', and the original-key metadata field - these carry no byte claim

a declared value CAN be satisfied by allowlist membership (the historical commit's blobs, the out-of-tree contract, and named external control files) without the accompanying descriptive reference being independently verified

an ABSOLUTE path whose basename is not uniquely in-tree is accepted if the value matches an in-tree or allowlisted blob - the deliberate external-control-file allowance, and the clearest way a contradiction could still in principle be absorbed

when several targets are present only the FIRST that resolves is authoritative; a later path-like sibling that does not resolve is not additionally faulted. Consequence: an object carrying BOTH a path and an affine {stem}_ref is judged on the affine ref alone, so a contradictory path sibling is not caught
the allowlist is a minimal, enumerated external-reference set, not a general escape hatch
